rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says idh reminds listeners of a definite incident even if they have forgotten it or departed from it.
rows.anchor: serves to remind people of an incident that they accept as a certain happening regardless of having forgotten it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With contextual indications, a singular address can encompass a plural audience.
rows.anchor: in the presence of concomitant indications an address in the singular encompasses plurality

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, the singular speaker addresses each person in the group individually.
rows.anchor: is addressing every person of the group individually

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi parses “from their loins” as a badal, or appositive, to the preceding expression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge concerns all Adam’s descendants through the Day of Judgement.
rows.anchor: it relates to all his progeny that will be born until the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event occurred before the descendants’ spirits were breathed into their bodies.
rows.anchor: was done at the time before these spirits were blown into their bodies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge required accepting God as Lord as well as God, not merely acknowledging Him as deity.
rows.anchor: God did not take a promise from the progeny of Adam (sws) that merely he was their God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs accepted God as deity but had other lords, although the pledge acknowledged God’s providence alone.
rows.anchor: the Arabs never rejected him being God; however, they had many Lords besides God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word meaning “lest” is omitted before the excuse clauses, yielding the precise sense of the passage.
rows.anchor: a word to the effect y (lest) is suppressed before

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is accountable for monotheism and innate guidance on the basis of the pledge, whether or not they received a prophet’s message.
rows.anchor: them on the basis of the afore-mentioned pledge whether he has received the message of a prophet or not

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving a prophet’s message adds proof and makes accountability twofold.
rows.anchor: In case he did, it will be a further burden of proof on him and his accountability will become two-fold

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a prophet’s message, a person still has no excuse regarding the obvious innate guidance of human nature.
rows.anchor: a person will not have an excuse regarding the obvious innate guidance he was provided by his nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancestral polytheism is no excuse; an external excuse cannot override the obvious guidance of human nature.
rows.anchor: ancestral polytheism will not be accepted as an excuse from a person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi supplies a suppressed coordinated clause: the explanation conclusively conveys truth so those wishing to repent from polytheism may do so.
rows.anchor: those who want to repent from polytheism can do so

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recounting the pledge is a further divine favour; those who persist in stubbornness must accept responsibility for its consequences.
rows.anchor: those who want to be adamant on their stubbornness should regard themselves responsible of its consequences

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an presents the pledge as a real happening, grounding accountability before God in His providence.
rows.anchor: mentioned this incident as a real happening

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings need not recall when or where; their innate cognizance of the pledge remains, while God reveals its unseen occasion, which only He knows, making this natural knowledge conclusive proof.
rows.anchor: its cognizance is found within human nature

rows.speaker: modern philosophers
rows.claim: Modern philosophers claim humanity began with polytheism, driven by fear of unseen forces amid calamities; as knowledge grew, people abandoned imagined deities and accepted one God.
rows.anchor: our modern philosophers say that human beings began their religion with polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects this philosophical account and says he refuted it in his commentary on al-Fātiḥah.
rows.anchor: I have refuted this view of these philosophers
